title: Finite-resolution measurement induces topological curvature defects in spacetime
summary: We show that regularizing $(2+1)$-dimensional Minkowski spacetime with a finite-resolution Gaussian probe, analogous to Weyl-Heisenberg (Gabor) signal analysis and related quantization, induces a curved geometry with a topological defect. The regularized metric replaces $r^2$ by $r^2+σ^2$ in the angular part, where $σ$ is the resolution scale from the width of the Gaussian probe. The resulting Gaussian curvature integrates to $-2π$, independently of $σ$. This curvature defines an effective stress-energy source with universal total energy $E_{\text{eff}}=-1/(4G)$.
